question: Which of the following chemical reactions is best described as double displacement reaction?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Na2SO4 (aq) + BaCl2 (aq) → BaSO4 (s) + 2NaCl (aq)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Double displacement reactions** involve the exchange of ions between two compounds to form two new compounds. These reactions typically occur in aqueous solutions.
 
• The given reaction **Na2SO4 (aq) + BaCl2 (aq) → BaSO4 (s) + 2NaCl (aq)** is a perfect example of a double displacement reaction, where the sulfate ions (SO4²⁻) from Na2SO4 combine with barium ions (Ba²⁺) from BaCl2 to form BaSO4, a precipitate.
 
• The reaction also results in the formation of sodium chloride (NaCl), which remains dissolved in the aqueous solution.
 
• This reaction demonstrates the principle of precipitation, where the insoluble compound BaSO4 forms as a solid and can be separated from the solution.
